name: "Freezer Friendly" Greek-Spiced Turkey & Rice Stuffed Peppers with Feta (Batch-Cooking)

instructions.primary_message: This recipe makes 2 (9 x 13-inch) baking pans of stuffed peppers or 12 servings.
Preheat oven to broil on high.
Using a strainer or colander, rinse the rice under cold, running water, then drain and transfer to a medium saucepan. Add water and salt, then bring the mixture to a boil over high heat.
instructions.secondary_message:
1 ½ cups basmati rice
3 cups water
½ tsp salt

instructions.primary_message: Meanwhile, wash and dry the fresh produce.
instructions.secondary_message:
1 small bunch fresh dill
1 small bunch Italian (flat-leaf) parsley
1 lemon

instructions.primary_message: Once the liquid comes to a boil, stir the mixture, cover the pan, and reduce heat to low. Cook rice until liquid is fully absorbed, 15-18 minutes. Once done, remove rice from the heat and let it stand, still covered, for 5 minutes. Transfer rice to a large bowl and set aside to cool slightly, stirring occasionally.

While the rice is cooking, trim, seed, and halve peppers lengthwise. Divide between two large baking sheet pans, drizzle with oil, and season with salt; arrange cut-side down. Working in batches, place baking sheets in the oven and broil, flipping once, until peppers are lightly charred and just tender, 6-8 minutes. Remove from oven.
instructions.secondary_message:
2 tbsp extra virgin olive oil
½ tsp salt
½ tsp black pepper

instructions.primary_message: Meanwhile, peel, halve, and small dice onions; peel and mince garlic. Place both in a small bowl and set aside.
Preheat a large skillet over medium high heat.

Once the skillet is hot, add oil and swirl to coat the bottom. Add turkey and spices; cook, breaking the meat apart with a spoon, until browned and crumbly, 6-7 minutes. Add to the bowl with the rice. (Reserve skillet with cooking juices for the next step.)
instructions.secondary_message:
2 tbsp extra virgin olive oil
2 lb lean ground turkey
1 tbsp paprika
1 tbsp oregano, dried
1 ¼ tsp salt
¾ tsp black pepper
¼ tsp cinnamon, ground

instructions.primary_message: Return skillet (with cooking juices) to medium-high heat, add more oil, and swirl to coat the bottom. Add onion, garlic, and salt; cook, stirring occasionally, until softened, 5-6 minutes.
instructions.secondary_message:
1 ½ tbsp extra virgin olive oil
¼ tsp salt

instructions.primary_message: Add tomatoes to the skillet and stir to combine. Continue to cook, stirring occasionally, until tomato sauce thickens slightly, 3-4 minutes more. Remove from heat.
Juice lemon into the skillet with the tomato sauce, then stir to combine. Let cool slightly, 10 minutes.
Meanwhile, shave dill and parsley leaves off the stems; discard stems and mince the leaves. Add herbs to the bowl with the rice.
When the tomato sauce has cooled, add to the bowl, along with feta, then stir to combine the filling.

Stuff each pepper halfway full with the rice filling, then using your hands or the back of a small spoon, push the filling into the deep crevices of each pepper before filling the rest of the way, mounding the rice on top. (Each pepper should hold 1/2-3/4 cup rice filling.)

Divide peppers between two 9 x 13-inch disposable foil pans, then top with additional feta and drizzle with oil. (If you have leftover filling, spread it out over the bottom of each pan before placing the peppers inside or reserve for another use.)
instructions.secondary_message:
1 (4 oz) pkg crumbled feta cheese
2 tbsp extra virgin olive oil

instructions.primary_message: STORING: Tightly cover each pan with aluminum foil, then wrap the whole pan with plastic wrap. Place in the freezer for up to 1 month. HEATING: For best results, thaw peppers in the fridge overnight, then remove plastic wrap. Place foil-covered pan(s) in a preheated 375°F oven and bake until heated through, 25-30 minutes. (If you'd prefer to bake after assembly, place stuffed peppers in a preheated 375°F oven, uncovered, until filling is heated through, 25-30 minutes.)
